link.per: law in force, share of covered firms production costs
link.group: covered firms; current producer applies to represented town businesses as a provisional adaptation
link.source: Demirer, Jimenez Hernandez, Li and Peng 2024, NBER Working Paper 32146; existing federal-data-privacy-law.ts CTO-approved European cost adaptation
link.rangeBasis: Existing cited adaptation 0.1%–0.6%; this is not claimed as a confidence interval. Center is within that existing interval. Team9 must verify reported quantity, units and US applicability.
why: An operative privacy law requires covered firms to change data handling and demonstrate compliance.
Firms allocate staff, systems and legal resources to those obligations.
Those resources add production costs; current stepTownFinances prices a share of payroll plus other costs.
Quarterly net earnings and cash subtract that actual recorded dollar cost.
Bedrock: the legal compliance duty consumes paid work and services; the firms cash books record those resources.

conditions.stronger: Compliance burden can depend on processing intensity, prior safeguards, scale and implementation; no interaction coefficient is supplied.
conditions.weaker: Prior compliant systems can reduce incremental burden; the cited EU range does not establish a US coefficient for each industry.
conditions.absent: No operative controlling yes law yields zero new compliance cost. Legal exemptions and US firm-specific coverage remain unmodeled, not permission to assume everyone covered.

link.reverseOnRepeal: The current producer stops future quarterly cost after operative repeal. Past expenditures and installed systems remain on the books; research has not established that every recurring compliance cost immediately disappears.
link.who: Firm organizations whose books incur covered production costs; owners can feel cash/debt effects. Employees are not presumed hired or laid off.
link.lagWhy: The legal duty is read at the quarterly finance review. Actual cost is saved on that quarter; immediate legal operation does not imply immediate hiring effects.
link.oneStep: Cash/credit affordability reaches bankruptcy/closure and recorded work status; generic hire affordability currently omits privacyCost, so no hiring elasticity is claimed.
link.blend: This cost is a distinct additive expense on actual production costs. Do not also multiply the same business cash or cost by this map factor. Other compliance duties need separate incremental cost evidence.
link.readiness: PROPOSED numeric addition for coordinator review; not yet integrated or activated. Direct reader must share its draw key; canonical saved amount+stamp pending exact caller ownership.

primarySourceRead.quote: This increase translates into only a 0.1–0.6% rise in overall production costs because data plays a relatively small role in firm production compared to computation.
primarySourceRead.quantity: Overall production cost rise, not a confidence interval, US legal rate or person job-loss probability.
primarySourceRead.observedContext: European firms responding to GDPR compared with comparable US firms; data/computation complementarity.
